questions.stem: What is the cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.text: The pancreas produces too much glucagon
The immune system destroys the beta cells that produce insulin
The liver stops storing glycogen
The body's cells stop responding to insulin

questions.explanation: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks and destroys the beta cells in the pancreas. Without these cells, the body cannot produce insulin, so blood glucose cannot be regulated.

options.text: By regular insulin injections
By diet and exercise alone
By taking glucagon tablets
By removing the pancreas

questions.explanation: Type 1 diabetes is treated with regular insulin injections (or an insulin pump) because the body cannot produce its own insulin. Patients must also monitor their blood glucose levels and manage their diet carefully.

questions.stem: What is the main characteristic of Type 2 diabetes?

options.text: The pancreas produces no insulin at all
The liver produces too much glucose
The kidneys cannot filter glucose from the blood
The body's cells become resistant to insulin

questions.explanation: In Type 2 diabetes, the body's cells become resistant to insulin, meaning they do not respond properly to it. The pancreas may also produce less insulin over time. Blood glucose levels therefore remain high.

questions.stem: Which risk factor is most strongly associated with developing Type 2 diabetes?

options.text: Being underweight
Having Type 1 diabetes as a child
Getting a viral infection
Being obese or overweight

questions.explanation: Obesity is the most significant risk factor for Type 2 diabetes. Excess body fat, particularly around the abdomen, is linked to increased insulin resistance. Other risk factors include lack of exercise, age, and family history.

questions.stem: Why might glucose be found in the urine of a person with untreated diabetes?

options.text: Because the kidneys have stopped working completely
Because insulin breaks down glucose in the kidneys
Because the kidneys are producing glucose
Because blood glucose is so high that the kidneys cannot reabsorb it all

questions.explanation: In untreated diabetes, blood glucose levels are very high. During filtration in the kidneys, so much glucose enters the filtrate that the transport proteins in the nephron become saturated and cannot reabsorb it all, so glucose appears in the urine.

questions.stem: At what age does Type 1 diabetes typically develop?

options.text: Only in newborn babies
Only in people over 60 years old
Only during pregnancy
Usually in childhood or adolescence

questions.explanation: Type 1 diabetes typically develops in childhood or adolescence, though it can occur at any age. It has a sudden onset and is not linked to lifestyle factors, unlike Type 2 diabetes which tends to develop later in life.

questions.stem: How can Type 2 diabetes often be managed in the early stages?

options.text: By insulin injections only
By changes to diet and increasing exercise
By having the pancreas removed
By taking antibiotics

questions.explanation: Type 2 diabetes can often be managed in its early stages through lifestyle changes such as eating a balanced diet, losing weight, and increasing physical activity. These measures help improve insulin sensitivity and control blood glucose levels.
